preconditions.expression: all(c.isdigit() for c in stdin.splitlines()[0]) and all(c.isdigit() for c in stdin.splitlines()[1]) and stdin.splitlines()[2].isdigit()
preconditions.description: Input consists of three lines: first line is integer l (as string), second line is integer r (as string), third line is integer n (as string).
Integer n is between 1 and 2000 inclusive.
Integers l and r have at most 801 digits each.
l is less than or equal to r.

postconditions.description: Output consists of two lines: first line is the maximum number of modest substrings (as string), second line is the lexicographically smallest string of length n.
The output string has length exactly n.
The output string consists only of digits.

postconditions.expression: max_count == int(stdout.splitlines()[0]) and max_count == count_modest_substrings(stdout.splitlines()[1], l, r)
postconditions.description: The first line of output is the maximum possible number of modest substrings in any string of length n.

postconditions.expression: all(s > 0 and int(s) >= int(l) and int(s) <= int(r) for s in get_all_substrings(stdout.splitlines()[1]))
postconditions.description: Every modest substring in the output string is a valid modest integer (no leading zeros).

postconditions.expression: not any(s == '0' and len(s) > 1 for s in get_all_substrings(stdout.splitlines()[1]))
postconditions.description: No modest substring has leading zeros.
The output string is lexicographically smallest among all strings with the maximum number of modest substrings.
